issues.title: Hardcoded devtools loading message text
issues.description: The rule requires all user-facing strings to be defined in web/i18n/en-US/ translation files and accessed via useTranslation hook. The code hardcodes 'Loading devtools...' directly in the JSX instead of using a translation key.
issues.rule_name: Frontend User-Facing Strings Must Use i18n Translations

issues.title: Devtools rendered before application children causes layout issues
issues.description: The TanStackDevtoolsLoader is now rendered before the children components in the QueryClientProvider. This reverses the intended rendering order from the original PR, which had devtools after children. When devtools mount first, they may inject DOM elements before the main application content is rendered, potentially causing layout shifts, visual flashes, or z-index conflicts. Devtools should be rendered as a sibling after main content to avoid interfering with the initial application layout and rendering.

issues.title: Missing error logging in TanStack devtools lazy import
issues.description: The TanStackDevtoolsLoader silently swallows import errors without logging them, making it impossible to debug why the devtools fail to load. This creates an inconsistent error handling pattern compared to the ReactScanLoader (in the same PR), which properly logs errors with console.error before returning a fallback component. When developers encounter issues with TanStack devtools not appearing, they will have no visibility into whether it's due to an import failure, missing dependencies, or other issues.

issues.title: console.error violates Frontend Code Must Not Use console Statements rule
issues.description: The ReactScanLoader uses console.error which directly violates Rule 25 from AGENTS.md added in this same PR. The rule explicitly states that production frontend code must avoid console.log, console.warn, and console.error statements as enforced by the no-console warning rule. This creates an inconsistency where the code violates a compliance rule that was just introduced, and creates inconsistent error handling compared to TanStackDevtoolsLoader which silently catches errors. The use of console statements in production code should be replaced with proper logging mechanisms.

issues.title: console.error used in frontend code
issues.description: Rule 25 prohibits console statements in frontend code. The added code logs an error with console.error when lazy-loading fails.
issues.rule_name: Frontend Code Must Not Use console Statements

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30318 - refactor(web): organize devtools components
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the React Scan and TanStack devtools into `web/app/components/devtools/{react-scan,tanstack}/` and adds a `Loader` component per tool. Each loader owns the `IS_DEV` gate, the `lazy()` import, and the `Suspense` boundary. `layout.tsx` now renders `<ReactScanLoader />` and `query-client.tsx` renders `<TanStackDevtoolsLoader />` in place of the inline lazy/IS_DEV code. The file moves are 100% similarity renames, so history is preserved.

The refactor is clean and does fix a real bundle issue: the base `layout.tsx` statically imported `react-scan`, which put that library into the production layout chunk even though `scan()` only ran in dev. With `scan.tsx` now behind a `lazy()` import, it becomes a separate chunk that is never requested in production. The remaining concerns are smaller: the module-scope `lazy(() => import(...))` is not gated by `IS_DEV`, so the dev-only chunks are still emitted in production builds; the two loaders handle import failures differently; the React Scan fallback renders visible text into the app body; and the loaders have no tests. The PR description also mentions a barrel `index.ts` that is not in the head commit.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Nothing here is a correctness or security blocker. The IS_DEV gating still works at runtime, the rename preserves history, and the lazy/Suspense wrapping is behaviorally the same as before for TanStack. The issues are a build-output nuance, inconsistent error handling, a visible dev-only fallback, and missing tests, all worth addressing but not merge-blocking.

architecture.overview:
In the base, the root layout statically imports `ReactScan` from `components/react-scan.tsx`, which imports the `react-scan` package at top level. `query-client.tsx` holds a module-level `lazy()` for `@/app/components/devtools` and gates rendering with an inline `IS_DEV &&` check. Both tools are therefore wired ad hoc from two different places, and React Scan's library code sits in the layout's eager import graph.

After this PR, each tool has a folder with an implementation file (`scan.tsx`, `devtools.tsx`) and a `loader.tsx`. The loader is a `'use client'` component that returns null unless `IS_DEV`, and otherwise renders the lazily-imported implementation inside `Suspense`. The layout and the query provider each render one loader and no longer know anything about the tool internals.
steps: Entry points are `web/app/layout.tsx` (the root server layout, which now renders `<ReactScanLoader />` inside `<body>`) and `web/context/query-client.tsx` (the client `TanstackQueryInitializer`, which now renders `<TanStackDevtoolsLoader />` inside `QueryClientProvider`).

Each loader in `react-scan/loader.tsx` and `tanstack/loader.tsx` declares a module-scope `lazy()` that dynamically imports its implementation file (`./scan` or `./devtools`), with a `.catch` that substitutes a null component.

At render time the loader checks `IS_DEV` and returns null in production. In development it renders the lazy component inside `Suspense`, which is the only place the implementation chunk is requested.
Implementation files are moved without content changes: `react-scan/scan.tsx` still calls `scan()` under `IS_DEV`, and `tanstack/devtools.tsx` still exports `TanStackDevtoolsWrapper`.

findings.title: Dev-only devtools chunks are still emitted in production builds
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx` and `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx`, the module-scope `lazy(() => import(...))` calls are not gated by `IS_DEV`, so Next.js still emits dev-only devtools chunks in production builds. Wrap each `lazy()` call in a compile-time `IS_DEV ? lazy(...) : () => null` check so the bundler can drop the dynamic import in production. Keep the existing `.catch` error fallbacks. Keep the runtime `if (!IS_DEV) return null` guard in the components. Verify the production build output no longer contains the react-scan or tanstack devtools chunks.

findings.title: Inconsistent error handling between the two loaders
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx`, the `.catch` on the lazy import (lines 6-11) silently returns a null component, while `react-scan/loader.tsx` logs with `console.error`. Make the TanStack loader log the error the same way, using a message like 'Failed to load TanStack devtools:'. Keep the null-component fallback so the app still renders.

findings.title: React Scan fallback renders visible text into the app in dev
findings.body:
The React Scan loader's `Suspense` fallback is `
Loading devtools...
`. It is rendered inside `` in `layout.tsx`, so every dev page load shows this text until the chunk resolves. The TanStack loader uses `fallback={null}`, so the two tools behave differently. Because the devtools are dev-only and the fallback is just a status string, the cleaner choice is `fallback={null}` to match TanStack and avoid a layout shift in the dev page. ::diff{file="web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx" lines="19-23"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx`, the Suspense fallback (around line 20) renders a visible 'Loading devtools...' div inside the app body rendered by `web/app/layout.tsx`. Change it to `fallback={null}` to match `tanstack/loader.tsx`, since React Scan renders no UI and the fallback only adds dev-only visible text.

findings.title: New loaders have no test coverage
findings.body: The PR adds two new components with branching behavior: the `IS_DEV` gate, the Suspense wrapping, and the import-failure fallback. None of this has tests, and the repo already has component tests such as `web/context/modal-context.test.tsx`. A small Vitest test for each loader would lock in the dev-only gating, which is the main behavior the PR is meant to guarantee, and would catch an accidental `IS_DEV` regression.
findings.fixPrompt: Add Vitest tests for `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx` and `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx`. Mock `@/config` so `IS_DEV` can be toggled. Assert that each loader renders nothing when `IS_DEV` is false and does not render its implementation. When `IS_DEV` is true, assert that the lazy implementation is rendered. Follow the setup style of `web/context/modal-context.test.tsx`.

findings.title: Barrel export described in the PR is not present
findings.body: The PR description says `web/app/components/devtools/index.ts` was simplified into clean barrel exports. No `index.ts` exists under `web/app/components/devtools/` at the head commit. The consumers import the loader files directly, which is fine, but the description should be corrected so reviewers are not looking for a file that is not there.
findings.fixPrompt: The PR description says `web/app/components/devtools/index.ts` was simplified into a barrel. That file does not exist at head. Either add the barrel if it was intended, or update the PR description to match the actual change, which has the loaders imported directly from `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader` and `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader`.

findings.title: Moving react-scan out of the layout's static import graph
findings.body:
In the base, `layout.tsx` statically imported `ReactScan` from `components/react-scan.tsx`, which imports `react-scan` at the top level. That put React Scan's library code into the eager layout graph even in production, where `scan()` never ran. This PR removes that static import. `react-scan` is now reached only through the lazy `./scan` chunk, which is a real reduction in the initial client JS for production. This is the part of the bundle claim in the PR description that is actually true.

::diff{file="web/app/layout.tsx" lines="8-11"}
findings.fixPrompt: No change needed. This is a note for reviewers: `web/app/layout.tsx` no longer statically imports react-scan, so the library is no longer part of the eager layout chunk.
